S01.kontekst: A fictional military educational institution, graduating class. State certification is one week away. The course head signs graduates' service appraisals, which are taken into account when assigning posts.

diiovi_osoby.opys: An officer and direct superior of the course cadets. Played by the user.
A cadet's parent speaking on behalf of all parents.
The course head's immediate superior.
Their appraisals influence their postings.

S01.sytuatsiia: After a parents' meeting, a committee representative hands you an envelope containing an outdoor equipment gift voucher worth considerably more than a token amount. 'It is from all the parents, to thank you for four years. This is our tradition; your predecessor accepted it too. People will be offended if you refuse.' You know not all parents contributed. The graduates' appraisals have not yet been signed.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: Refusal offends people expressing sincere thanks. Acceptance casts doubt on every subsequent decision about cadets.
Some parents did not contribute to the gift, but the course head's decisions affect everyone.

vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do with the envelope?

varianty.tekst: Accept: it is a collective gift from parents, you requested nothing, and you will write honest appraisals anyway.

naslidky.odrazu: The conversation ends warmly; the parents are pleased.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Cadets learn about the voucher. Every appraisal, even a fair one, now appears to follow a gift.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The gift relates to service, so restrictions apply regardless of value. Tasks are not immediately affected, but trust falls because decisions can now be attributed to the gift.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Relations with parents are preserved, but future impartiality is questioned. Good intentions do not remove the problem: the gift relates to service (Article 23(1)), and decisions favouring a donor within three years are deemed to involve an actual conflict of interest (Article 23(4)).

varianty.tekst: Thank the parents and refuse, explaining the rules. Suggest a letter of thanks to the institution's head. Report the offer to the faculty head in writing.

naslidky.odrazu: An awkward pause. Some parents view the refusal as arrogance.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Next year another parents' committee asks in advance how to express gratitude. No graduate appraisal is challenged on this ground.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Article 24 procedures are followed. Trust grows slowly: few witness the refusal, and some parents feel offended.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 24 requires refusal, witnesses where possible and written notification to the superior. The cost is tension with some parents. Discuss how to refuse without devaluing their gratitude.

varianty.tekst: Refuse verbally and tell no one, to avoid making an issue of it.

naslidky.odrazu: The envelope is returned; nobody knows.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A month later, parents' chat messages claim the course head received the usual gift. There is no record of your refusal.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The essential step is taken: the gift is refused. Without written notification there is no evidence, and leadership remains unaware of the tradition.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Refusal is essential, but Article 24(1)(4) also requires written notification. Without it, refusal cannot be demonstrated and leadership receives no signal to change the tradition across courses.

varianty.tekst: Accept, then immediately pass the voucher to volunteers supporting a brigade where graduates serve.

naslidky.odrazu: Parents are pleased and volunteers grateful.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The course knows only that the head accepted a gift. Few see where it went afterwards.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Funds support a good cause, but the gift was received personally; passing it to others does not change that.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The intention is good, but the problem arises upon receipt, regardless of later use. Giving it to volunteers is not the procedure for gifts to the state (Article 23(3), Cabinet Resolution No. 1195). Cadets whose parents did not contribute see the same as in option A.

vuzly.tekst: A month later, a graduate challenges his posting. His complaint says his parents refused to contribute to the gift and his appraisal is weaker than his peers'. The faculty head summons you.
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you tell the faculty head?

varianty.tekst: Disclose the voucher, notify the faculty head in writing, draw up a record and request another officer's review of this graduate's appraisal.

naslidky.odrazu: An uncomfortable conversation. The faculty head orders a review.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The review confirms some comments and changes others. The complaint is considered on its merits.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Openness permits correction, but Article 24(2)'s one-working-day reporting deadline has passed.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Openness cannot undo the past, but allows someone without a private interest to review the appraisal. The gift should have been reported within one working day (Article 24(2)); some harm cannot now be repaired.

varianty.tekst: Say all appraisals are objective and do not mention the voucher.

naslidky.odrazu: The complaint is assessed without a crucial fact.
naslidky.vidkladeni: If the voucher emerges later, every appraisal for the course will be questioned.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The review is faster but based on incomplete information; risks to trust in all course decisions grow.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Silence extends the problem from one graduate to the entire course. The law already treats decisions favouring the donor as taken under an actual conflict of interest (Article 23(4)); concealment changes nothing.

normy.yak_zastosovuietsia: The course head is a military official by virtue of command responsibilities and is subject to Articles 23–24.
A service-related gift is prohibited regardless of value (paragraph 1). Decisions favouring the donor within three years involve an actual conflict of interest (paragraph 4).
Procedure when a gift is offered or has already been received.
Removal from decision-making: another officer reviews the appraisal.
The procedure concerns gifts to the state or an institution; handing a gift to volunteers does not legitimise receipt.
NACP explanations and examples of prohibited and permitted gifts.
Explains why the course head is a military official.
Unverified. Administrative liability for breaching Article 23 may be mentioned on the basis of NACP guidance, without specifying penalties.

S01.zastosovnist: Articles 23–24 apply to the course head as a military official. They do not apply to cadets' parents: offering the gift in this scenario does not breach these rules for them, but accepting it does for the officer. Whether the voucher falls within generally accepted hospitality under Article 23(2) is irrelevant: the exception does not apply in paragraph 1 cases.
porady: When offered a gift, refuse, identify the donor where possible, involve witnesses and notify your immediate superior in writing (Article 24(1)).
If a gift has been received or discovered, notify your superior in writing within one working day and draw up a record (Article 24(2)).
If unsure whether a gift is permissible, request written NACP advice (Article 24(5)).
Direct gratitude to the institution: a letter of thanks or an institutional gift documented under the procedure for gifts to the state.
pytannia_dlia_obhovorennia: Would your decision change if the gift were presented after postings? Why?
How can you refuse without making parents feel their gratitude is devalued?
Who should change the tradition so the next course head does not face the same situation?

S02.nazva: The candidate is your comrade's son
S02.kontekst: A department at a fictional military educational institution is selecting three cadets for a three-month placement in a partner country. Ranking combines academic results (40%), a language test (30%) and a panel interview (30%, scored by each member). The list is due on Friday.

diiovi_osoby.rol: Senior lecturer and selection panel member
diiovi_osoby.opys: An officer and one of three panel members. Played by the user.
The senior lecturer's immediate superior.
The son of the lecturer's comrade, with whom the lecturer served and maintains a family friendship.
Eight cadets competing for the same three places.

S02.sytuatsiia: The evening before the interviews, you notice your comrade's son among the nine candidates. He is strong: fourth on academic and language results, so the interview will decide whether he makes the top three. Your comrade has not called or asked for anything. If you withdraw from the panel, only two members remain and the chair will probably postpone the interviews until Monday, after the partner's deadline.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_a: Friendship and loyalty to a comrade
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: The candidate may deserve selection, but the assessor cannot prove friendship did not influence the score.
Managing the conflict of interest may jeopardise the partner's deadline.

vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do before the interviews?

varianty.tekst: Notify the department head in writing of a potential conflict of interest and request removal from assessing this candidate or replacement on the panel.

naslidky.odrazu: The head is displeased at finding a replacement overnight. Interviews are delayed two hours.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The cadet reaches the top three. When another candidate appeals, your report and the head's decision provide evidence of impartiality.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Procedure is followed and results withstand appeal, at the cost of delay and the superior's displeasure.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Private interest includes friendship, not just family (Article 1). Reporting does not mean you are biased: it enables management measures (Articles 28–29) and protects both you and the candidate.

varianty.tekst: Participate but deliberately assess your comrade's son more harshly to avoid criticism.

naslidky.odrazu: Nobody notices and the schedule is maintained.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The cadet finishes fifth and misses the placement. If the friendship emerges, all your scores will be questioned.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The deadline is met, but assessment is biased in the opposite direction.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Impartiality means assessing without private influence, rather than compensating through severity. Private interest still affected the decision, to the candidate's detriment.

varianty.tekst: Leave the room during this candidate's interview without explanation and do not score him.

naslidky.odrazu: The chair is surprised but interviews continue. Two members assess this candidate.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Different numbers of assessors lead to inconsistent averages and an appeal against the method. No written removal decision exists: you left on your own initiative.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You avoided deciding under a conflict, but left the procedure vulnerable.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 28(1) and (3) require notification and a management decision by the superior. Leaving without that decision leaves the procedure vulnerable and colleagues without an explanation.

varianty.tekst: Do nothing: your comrade is not a close person under the statutory definition, so there is no conflict.

naslidky.odrazu: Interviews run on time. You give his son a high score, and he genuinely answers well.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The cadet reaches the top three. The next stage shows what follows.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The deadline is met, but the potential conflict remains unmanaged.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A comrade is outside Article 1's definition of close persons, but private interest is broader and includes friendship. A potential conflict exists even if the score is deserved.

vuzly.tekst: Two weeks later, another candidate's mother finds social media photos of your families together and files a complaint. The department head asks why you did not report the relationship.
vuzly.zapytannia: How do you respond?

varianty.tekst: Acknowledge underestimating the situation and request recalculation without your score.

naslidky.odrazu: The panel recalculates scores.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The cadet remains in the top three, but this must now be proved retrospectively and the placement begins late.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Acknowledgment permits verification, but time and some trust are lost.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Admitting the error enables review. The cadet might have succeeded without your score, but this now needs retrospective proof.

varianty.tekst: Insist that friendship did not influence your assessment and the score was deserved.

naslidky.odrazu: The head escalates the complaint.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The review drags on. A cadet who might have won fairly falls under suspicion alongside you.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The score may be deserved, but impartiality is hard to prove without disclosure.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A potential conflict depends on the private interest, not the outcome. Without reporting, impartiality is difficult to demonstrate and suspicion also harms the cadet.

normy.yak_zastosovuietsia: Private interest includes friendship; definition of a potential conflict of interest.
Notify the immediate superior by the next working day; the superior decides management measures.
Removal from decision-making as external conflict management.
Requirement of impartiality.
All assessors of academic results must act without a conflict or after it has been managed.
Avoiding conflicts is a fundamental academic integrity principle.
Criteria for determining whether the senior lecturer is a military official.

S02.zastosovnist: Article 28 duties apply to persons listed in Article 3(1)(1) and (2). Whether a senior lecturer is a military official depends on organisational, managerial, administrative or economic duties, or specific authorisation (NACP Clarification No. 4, question 194); a specialist should clarify this. Regardless, every academic assessor must avoid or manage conflicts (Academic Integrity Law, Article 9(2)).
porady: Report an actual or potential conflict by the next working day (Article 28(1)(2)).
Pending a management decision, do not act or decide under an actual conflict (Article 28(1)(3)).
The superior decides management measures within two working days (Article 28(3)).
If in doubt, seek NACP clarification (Article 28(5)).
pytannia_dlia_obhovorennia: Where is the boundary between colleague, neighbour, former classmate and comrade? What makes a relationship a private interest?
How should selection procedures accommodate one member's conflict without missing deadlines?
Is it fair to the cadet that other people assess him because of his father's friendship?

S03.kontekst: A cadet company from a fictional military educational institution has completed a field exercise. A commission prepares the fuel write-off report. A fourth-year cadet serving as deputy platoon commander is a commission member.

diiovi_osoby.rol: Fourth-year cadet, deputy platoon commander and commission member
diiovi_osoby.opys: Kept personal refuelling records during the exercise. Played by the user.
A combat-experienced officer respected throughout the company; chairs the commission.
Refuelled vehicles during the exercise.

diiovi_osoby.rol: Institution's authorised corruption prevention and detection officer
diiovi_osoby.opys: Receives reports through internal channels.

S03.sytuatsiia: Your records show that company vehicles consumed about half the fuel listed in the draft report. The company commander explains: 'The rest went to a generator for volunteers delivering aid to our troops. There are no documents and there will not be any. Sign it; it is for a good cause.' A driver privately says some fuel was drained into cans and he does not know where they went. You cannot verify either account. The report must be signed today.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: Signing preserves peace but confirms figures your records indicate are false.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_a: Trust in a good cause and the commander's combat experience
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: The fuel may genuinely have supported the frontline, but you cannot verify this and the signature is yours.
Reporting may harm company relationships; silence may allow misconduct to continue.

vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do with the report?

varianty.tekst: Sign: the commander knows what he is doing and the purpose is probably good.

naslidky.odrazu: The commander thanks you; the company remains calm.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A routine accounting inspection discovers the discrepancy. Your signature is on an inaccurate document regardless of where the fuel went.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Relationships are preserved for now, but your signature confirms figures you believe false.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: You assume responsibility for a document contradicted by your own records. A good cause does not make accounts truthful. Discuss separately whether the request is an order and whether it is manifestly criminal (Internal Service Regulations, Articles 30 and 36).

varianty.tekst: Refuse to sign and explain why, but tell nobody else.

naslidky.odrazu: A tense conversation. The commander says someone else will sign.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Another cadet signs. If fuel was stolen, it continues; otherwise the matter remains unexplained.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You avoided endorsing false records, but concerns remain within the company.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Refusing matters, but possible misconduct remains unresolved. You may report it; the law protects reporters who believe their information is reliable.

varianty.tekst: Refuse to sign and report possible misconduct to the authorised officer or Unified Whistleblower Reporting Portal, anonymously if needed.

naslidky.odrazu: Nobody in the company knows who reported. You feel anxious.
naslidky.vidkladeni: An investigation begins. The next stage shows what follows.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You refused a false document and referred concerns to people able to investigate; relationship consequences remain unknown.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: You report possible facts, not a verdict. Investigation establishes events. Whistleblower status includes information learned through service or study and provides confidentiality and protection from retaliation (Articles 1, 53-4 and 53-5).

varianty.tekst: Sign but photograph your records just in case.

naslidky.odrazu: No conflict; you retain copies.
naslidky.vidkladeni: An investigation would show that you knew about the discrepancy but signed anyway.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: An attempt at self-protection without addressing the problem.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Copies do not cancel your signature; they demonstrate prior doubt. This protects you less than it seems and changes nothing for the company.

vuzly.tekst: The investigation finds that some fuel went to volunteers and some was drained without records. The commander is transferred. Some company members suspect who reported and stop talking to you.
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do?

varianty.tekst: Ask the authorised officer for help with pressure: whistleblower rights include protection against adverse measures.

naslidky.odrazu: The officer records your concern and speaks with course command.
naslidky.vidkladeni: There is no overt harassment, but peers remain distant for months.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Rights are protected, but law cannot restore interpersonal trust.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 53-4(1) covers adverse measures beyond dismissal. Law cannot compel peers to speak to you: restoring collective trust is a separate command responsibility.

varianty.tekst: Speak openly with the platoon: explain why you could not sign without disclosing investigative details.

naslidky.odrazu: The discussion is difficult; some disagree.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Several peers admit they would also have refused. Tension gradually eases.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Explaining your choice rather than judging the commander helps restore trust.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: You may disclose your own reporting role, but should not reveal investigation details or other participants' information.

varianty.tekst: Request transfer to another platoon.

naslidky.odrazu: Your personal stress subsides.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The company concludes that reporters must leave. Future misconduct goes unreported.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You feel better, but colleagues see reporting as costly for the reporter.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Discuss transfer with the authorised officer so it does not appear punitive: otherwise the message is that the reporter must leave.

normy.yak_zastosovuietsia: Whistleblower status includes information learned through service or study.
Cadets are excluded from Article 3(1)(1)(g); officials' duties are not imposed on them.
Officials' 24-hour reporting duty does not apply to the cadet, but may apply to others involved.
Internal channels and the Unified Whistleblower Reporting Portal, including anonymous reports.
Whistleblowers choose their reporting channel.
Protection from adverse measures connected to reporting.
Confidentiality of the whistleblower's identity.
Limits of the duty to obey orders.
Commander's responsibility for an order and its legality.

S03.zastosovnist: Military higher education cadets are excluded under Article 3(1)(1)(g), so officials' 24-hour reporting duty (Article 53(6)) does not apply. Reporting rights and whistleblower safeguards do apply: Article 1 includes information learned during service or study. Whether a request to sign is an order, and manifestly criminal, is deliberately left for discussion and specialist review. Criminal Code provisions and fuel write-off procedures are not reproduced here.
porady: Choose an internal channel (authorised officer or head), regular channel (NACP, anti-corruption or investigation bureaus, police or prosecutor), or external channel (media or civil society) under Articles 1 and 53-2(1).
The Unified Whistleblower Reporting Portal accepts anonymous reports (Article 53-1(2)).
Report possible facts rather than proving guilt; investigators establish the circumstances.
A whistleblower's identity must not be disclosed to persons concerned by the report (Article 53-5(1)).
pytannia_dlia_obhovorennia: Would your decision change if you knew all fuel supported frontline volunteers?
How does loyalty to a commander differ from loyalty to the service?
How could the commander support volunteers without imposing this choice on subordinates?

audytoriia: educators discussing AI rules and workload
S04.kontekst: Third year at a fictional military educational institution. A tactics term-paper grade contributes to the ranking used to choose graduate postings. The department announced its rules in advance: AI may help with source searches, outlining and editing, but each use must be disclosed in the introduction; cadets must write the analysis themselves.

diiovi_osoby.opys: The term-paper author. Played by the user.
Advises taking the easy route and has already submitted an AI-generated paper.
Assesses the work and conducts its defence.
Examines reports of academic integrity violations.

S04.sytuatsiia: Duty shifts and two field exercises left you behind. Ten hours remain before submission and only an outline is ready. A classmate writes: 'Generate it with a chatbot, rewrite it in your own words and do not disclose AI use. Everyone does it; detectors catch nothing.' You know two classmates have already done this.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_a: Honesty with yourself and the instructor
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: An honest choice distinguishes you from those using AI without disclosure and raises whether to remain silent about them.
Overload is real and rankings affect postings, but rankings are fair only when everyone follows the same rules.

vuzly.zapytannia: How do you prepare the paper?

varianty.tekst: Generate the main text, rewrite it in your own words and omit AI disclosure.

naslidky.odrazu: The paper is ready on time and reads smoothly.
naslidky.vidkladeni: At the defence you cannot explain a conclusion. One listed source does not exist: the model invented it.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Time is saved, but the work is no longer yours and the invented source adds another violation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Publishing generated text as your own without disclosure is a distinct violation (Article 29). An invented source may constitute fabrication (Article 27). The main loss is the subject you never learned.

varianty.tekst: Write the paper yourself, using AI for outlining and language checks; disclose exactly how you used it in the introduction.

naslidky.odrazu: A sleepless night. The paper is shorter and weaker than intended.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Your grade is lower than classmates', but you answer every defence question. A classmate approaches the next day, in the next stage.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Rules are followed, at the cost of a lower ranking affecting your posting.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The choice complies with departmental rules and disclosure requirements (Article 8(4)). Honesty has a real ranking cost here; discuss it openly, including with the department.

varianty.tekst: Explain your duty shifts and field exercises to the instructor and request a few extra days.

naslidky.odrazu: The instructor allows two days but lowers the maximum grade for late submission.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Three more cadets request the same. The department sees the conflict between duty schedules and coursework. A classmate approaches the next day, in the next stage.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: No rules are broken and a systemic issue becomes visible, at the cost of delay and a lower maximum grade.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: You reveal a systemic problem, but not everyone may have this opportunity and some may see favouritism. Fairness depends on equivalent extensions for equivalent circumstances.

varianty.tekst: Take a senior cadet's paper from last year on the same topic and rework it.

naslidky.odrazu: The paper is ready within hours.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A similarity check finds last year's paper in the department repository.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Fast, but it is someone else's work without attribution.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Reproducing another's work without attribution is plagiarism (Article 24); work done by another person lacks independence (Article 31) and is treated as not completed.

vuzly.tekst: Results are announced. The classmate who submitted undisclosed AI-generated work scored higher than you. He writes: 'Do not report me, all right?'
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do?

varianty.tekst: Remain silent: it is his responsibility.

naslidky.odrazu: Class relationships do not change.
naslidky.vidkladeni: More classmates do this next semester. The posting rankings become distorted for you too.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You committed no violation, but the distorted ranking persists.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 37 gives those with evidence a right to report. Whether the classmate's earlier advice constituted inducement that you had a duty to report (Article 34) remains for discussion.

varianty.tekst: Speak privately and suggest he tell the instructor himself about his AI use.

naslidky.odrazu: He is angry but promises to consider it.
naslidky.vidkladeni: He approaches the instructor. The grade is reduced, but the matter closes without complaints.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: He has a chance to correct matters himself, preserving class relationships.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Admission allows the sanction to be determined without the full review procedure (Article 38(2)); this is less painful than a complaint.

varianty.tekst: Notify the academic integrity officer and provide the evidence you have: his chat messages.

naslidky.odrazu: The officer accepts the report for review.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Review takes weeks. Some classmates call you an informer; others silently support you.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You exercise your reporting right; class relationships will probably deteriorate.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 37 permits reporting with verifiable facts. A violation is established only after the required procedure (Article 17(3)).

normy.yak_zastosovuietsia: General duty of academic integrity, referring to the Academic Integrity Law.
Academic integrity values: honesty, trust, fairness and responsibility.
Independent work unless assistance or tools are permitted.
Duty to disclose AI-generated material.
Dishonest use of AI-generated results.
Fabrication of data or facts.
Academic plagiarism.
Work completed without required independence.
Inducement and the duties of the person approached.
Right to report a violation.
Simplified procedure when a learner admits a violation.
Presumption of academic integrity.

S04.zastosovnist: The Academic Integrity Law applies to all learners, including cadets. Internal institutional rules determine specific sanctions, which are not listed here. A specialist should assess whether the advice to generate and conceal constitutes inducement under Article 34. If so, the cadet must refuse and notify the authorised body or officer by the next working day.
porady: Read departmental AI rules before starting: permitted uses and disclosure requirements.
Disclose what AI did and which tool was used (Article 8(4)).
Verify every suggested source: models invent references.
If service duties prevent timely completion, speak to the instructor before the deadline.

Is it fair that honesty costs ranking places? What could the department change?
Does the classmate's advice constitute inducement, and what follows for you?

S05.nazva: A truck for a good cause
audytoriia: officers responsible for property and transport
S05.kontekst: Cadets and instructors at a fictional military educational institution collected two generators and camouflage nets for a brigade where last year's graduates serve. The carrier cancelled on Friday. The brigade needs delivery by Sunday.

diiovi_osoby.opys: An officer responsible for the institution's trucks and military drivers. Played by the user.
A colleague respected by cadets.
A subordinate of the support service chief.

diiovi_osoby.rol: Deputy institutional head for rear services
diiovi_osoby.opys: The support chief's immediate superior; away on business but reachable.

S05.sytuatsiia: The coordinator asks for a truck and driver for Saturday 'unofficially'; volunteers will pay for fuel. Authorising the journey through an order and route approval would take several days. The truck would otherwise stand idle over the weekend. 'You know who this is for,' the coordinator says.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: The purpose is worthy, but property belongs to the state and can be used only within authorised powers.
The lawful route may take longer than the brigade can wait.
An unofficial trip exposes both you and the driver following your instructions to risk.

vuzly.zapytannia: What do you decide?

varianty.tekst: Provide the truck and driver unofficially: just once, for a good cause.

naslidky.odrazu: Volunteers are delighted; the cargo leaves on Saturday morning.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The next stage shows what happened on the road.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Delivery is fast and colleagues grateful, but property is used outside an official task without an authorised decision.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The worthy purpose makes this tempting. Article 22(1) prohibits using state property for private interests. Whether volunteer delivery is a private interest is debatable; absence of authorisation and documents is not. Your subordinate follows an undocumented instruction.

varianty.tekst: Refuse: official vehicles are for official tasks only.

naslidky.odrazu: The coordinator is offended and cargo remains at the institution.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Another carrier delivers a week later. Colleagues say rear services care only about paperwork.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The rule is applied equally and property and driver are protected, but aid is late and nobody sought a lawful solution.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Refusal without seeking alternatives looks indifferent and weakens trust in rules. Article 42 also requires preventing inefficient use of state property: asking whether a lawful route exists is worthwhile.

varianty.tekst: Call the deputy head, report the situation and request a written decision on authorising the trip as an official task.

naslidky.odrazu: The deputy asks until evening to consult a lawyer.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The trip is authorised on Monday and delivered Tuesday, two days late; alternatively, permission is refused and you seek another route.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The authorised person decides and bears responsibility, at the cost of speed.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The person issuing the order is responsible under Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations. Whether this trip can be authorised depends on internal rules; the scenario deliberately leaves that open.

varianty.tekst: Decline official transport but help find another carrier or use your own vehicle on your day off.

naslidky.odrazu: You spend Saturday making calls and travelling.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Cargo arrives Sunday. Next time volunteers again approach you personally.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Official and personal roles are separated and aid arrives, at your expense and time.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Official vehicles are protected while aid arrives. The cost is your own time and resources: this solution cannot scale into a service-wide rule.

vuzly.tekst: Saturday, 14:00. The truck is stopped at a checkpoint: the driver has neither an order nor a journey sheet. He calls you to ask what to say.
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you tell the driver?

varianty.tekst: Tell the driver to speak truthfully, come personally, accept responsibility and report to the deputy head.

naslidky.odrazu: The truck is held for hours; another vehicle takes the cargo to volunteers.
naslidky.vidkladeni: You face an internal inquiry. The driver is not punished because you issued the instruction.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: You do not shift consequences to a subordinate, but delivery becomes harder.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Responsibility for the instruction and its legality lies with whoever issued it (Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations), rather than the subordinate following it.

varianty.tekst: Ask the driver to claim official business and say the documents were left at the unit.

naslidky.odrazu: The truck is released.
naslidky.vidkladeni: An inspection checks departure logs a week later. The discrepancy now involves both you and the driver.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Misuse is compounded by dishonesty involving a subordinate.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: You force the driver to choose between lying and disobeying your instruction, a choice he should never have faced.

S06.nazva: Warehouse audit: family ties and shortages
S06.kontekst: A security and defence unit is deployed in its operational area. The authorised corruption prevention officer conducts a routine internal check of food stock write-offs and actual holdings at the combined field warehouse.

diiovi_osoby.opys: A unit officer responsible for compliance with anti-corruption legislation and the operation of internal reporting channels. Played by the user.
The authorised officer's direct superior: a highly respected combat officer with a personal interest in protecting his brother.
A lieutenant colonel and the unit commander's brother, directly subordinate to a close person; responsible for supplies.
A junior officer with material accountability, subordinate to the logistics chief.

S06.sytuatsiia: You discover systematic shortages of food rations and long-life specialist rations worth over UAH 480,000. Dispatch records show deliveries to companies, but frontline units refuse to acknowledge property they never received. The warehouse chief admits dispatching goods on verbal instructions from the logistics chief, the unit commander's brother. The commander summons you behind closed doors: 'We are fighting hard and our people are exhausted. Your paperwork will get my brother suspended, freeze supply accounts and paralyse the brigade. Record it as combat losses from last Tuesday's mortar attack, or your service in this unit is over.'

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_b: Misguided institutional loyalty and continuity of combat supplies
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: A truthful report stops theft but risks paralysing support services through conflict with the command. Recording combat losses avoids the commander's anger but makes the officer complicit in a criminal offence.

tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_a: The corruption prevention officer's professional duty
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.tsinnist_b: Personal safety and keeping one's post
tsinnosti_v_konflikti.poiasnennia: Resisting the commander leads to disciplinary persecution and threats of transfer to dangerous sectors. Silence destroys personnel's trust in the integrity function.

vuzly.zapytannia: What is your initial decision in the unit commander's office?

varianty.tekst: Firmly refuse to falsify records, register the official audit report in the headquarters incoming correspondence log and hand the commander a copy against signature.

naslidky.odrazu: The report is officially recorded by unit headquarters; the commander orders you out of his office.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The commander issues a severe reprimand for alleged abuse of authority and orders your deployment to a forward observation post.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Uncompromising compliance with the duty to document misconduct immediately escalates the internal conflict and complicates the authorised officer's further work.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The decision meets basic anti-corruption standards (Article 44 of the Law and Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations). You refused complicity in official forgery. Faced with threatened disciplinary retaliation, it is critical to activate institutional whistleblower protection mechanisms.

varianty.tekst: Offer the commander and his brother 48 hours to make good the shortages without registering an official audit report, to preserve the unit's supplies.

naslidky.odrazu: The commander agrees to a pause; the immediate conflict temporarily subsides.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Within two days, the logistics chief tries to force company senior NCOs to sign backdated fictitious statements, threatening to withhold fuel for combat missions.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: A private arrangement creates the illusion of a quick solution but opens the way to blackmailing subordinate troops and forging official records.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: An unlawful compromise endangers the NCOs and breaches requirements for an immediate response to corruption offences (Article 42). The commander's private interest remains unmanaged.

varianty.tekst: Immediately use secure external channels to report the offence, pressure and conflict of interest to the NACP and Military Law Enforcement Service as a whistleblower.

naslidky.odrazu: The NACP Unified Whistleblower Reporting Portal registers the report and assigns a unique number.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The Military Law Enforcement Service initiates an urgent inspection, but a hunt for the 'traitor' begins inside the unit, generating suspicion and tension among officers.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Whistleblower status provides direct protection against dismissal or punishment, but the lack of a prior internal record alienates colleagues.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: These actions comply with Articles 53-1 and 53-2 of the Law on Prevention of Corruption. You acquire whistleblower status. Be prepared for psychological pressure and attempts at internal isolation.

varianty.tekst: Prepare an interim report describing only part of the shortage as an accounting error during relocation, leaving the logistics chief to decide how to write off the rest.

naslidky.odrazu: Pleased with your 'flexibility', the commander signs the report and promises to support your next promotion in rank.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A surprise higher-headquarters inspection a month later uncovers the entire theft scheme; your falsified wording becomes the subject of a Military Law Enforcement Service investigation.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Deliberate distortion of report findings and complicity in concealing losses to the state.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The apparent tactical gain is outweighed by a complete loss of integrity and liability for official negligence or forgery (Article 42). The officer has lost independence and become dependent on the offenders.

vuzly.tekst: The unit commander has issued a severe reprimand for your alleged failure to perform official duties and is preparing your urgent transfer to a frontline rifle company. The logistics chief seals the warehouse and denies you access for a further inspection.
vuzly.zapytannia: What legal steps do you take to protect yourself against the commander's improper pressure?

varianty.tekst: Submit a formal complaint to the NACP and Military Law Enforcement Service requesting whistleblower protection under Article 53-4(1), including an order to revoke the disciplinary penalty and suspend the transfer.

naslidky.odrazu: The NACP issues a binding notice to the military authority that persecuting the authorised officer for performing anti-corruption duties is unacceptable.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Higher headquarters suspends the transfer order and commissions a comprehensive audit of the unit's logistics service.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Effective use of specialist anti-corruption mechanisms to counter informal and disciplinary pressure by the command.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: The Law guarantees that a whistleblower and authorised officer cannot be disciplined or subjected to other adverse measures because of a report (Article 53-4(1)). The NACP notice protects your rights.

varianty.tekst: Report personally to the operational command's deputy commander for logistics, documenting direct subordination between close persons (Article 27) and deliberate obstruction of the audit.

naslidky.odrazu: Operational command sends an independent rear-services commission to verify the facts.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The commission confirms that the brothers' service as commander and logistics chief violates the restrictions.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Escalating a breach of restrictions on close persons serving together to higher military leadership.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Article 27 expressly prohibits direct subordination of close persons. Notifying higher command allows the conflict of interest to be resolved systematically (Articles 28 and 29).

varianty.tekst: Try to settle the conflict through the deputy commander for moral and psychological support: offer to postpone the audit until next quarter in return for revoking the reprimand.

naslidky.odrazu: The reprimand is temporarily withdrawn for revision.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The logistics chief uses the time to rewrite all original receipt records, while your reputation as a principled officer suffers.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Private deals replace legal measures, erode integrity and allow evidence of the offence to be destroyed.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Abandoning institutional protection under Article 53-4 for a verbal settlement with offenders strips the authorised officer of independence and creates opportunities to destroy evidence.

vuzly.tekst: Forty-eight hours have passed. A combat company senior NCO shows you a statement he signed under pressure from the logistics chief, claiming his company received and used 600 field rations the soldiers never saw. The NCO asks for protection: he is being threatened with prosecution for disobedience.
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do now that your compromise has led to pressure on subordinate service members?

varianty.tekst: Immediately secure the forged statement, obtain the NCO's written account of the pressure and send an urgent report of abuse of authority to the Military Law Enforcement Service and prosecutor.

naslidky.odrazu: The NCO feels protected by the law; military law enforcement investigators arrive within 24 hours.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Warehouse records are seized and the logistics chief is suspended from duty.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Correcting the earlier mistake by immediately protecting a subordinate service member and lawfully documenting abuse.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A decisive move to formal proceedings saves personnel from false allegations and brings the matter back under Article 28 of the Law and Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations.

varianty.tekst: Confront the logistics chief: demand that he personally return the statement and stop intimidating NCOs, or you will escalate the scandal to the brigade commander.

naslidky.odrazu: The logistics chief stops pressuring the NCO but begins destroying electronic register copies.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Some evidence is lost; at a meeting, the commander accuses you of undermining trust among officers.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: A personal dispute without official law enforcement involvement gives the offender time to conceal the evidence.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Warning an offender that you intend to report them without formally securing the property leads to the loss of original records (Article 42).

varianty.tekst: Advise the company NCO to remain silent and avoid conflict with command, hoping the shortage will disappear from the books after the unit rotates.

naslidky.odrazu: The NCO leaves disappointed and demoralised.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Rumours spread across the brigade that the corruption prevention officer protects the commander's family network and forces soldiers to take the blame.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Silence leaves the subordinate without support and undermines trust in the corruption prevention service.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Encouraging acceptance of forged statements destroys the whistleblowing function and makes the officer morally complicit in a criminal offence (Article 42 of the Law; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

vuzly.tekst: Following your report, the NACP has registered proceedings and the Military Law Enforcement Service has arrived to seize records. The commander convenes an officers' meeting, alleging that someone is sending denunciations to the rear to disrupt combat operations, and demands that the anonymous reporter be publicly identified.
vuzly.zapytannia: What position do you take at the unit officers' meeting?

varianty.tekst: Speak openly at the meeting: state that you submitted the report officially as the authorised officer, within the law, to stop theft of supplies intended for the frontline; remind everyone of liability for whistleblower retaliation.

naslidky.odrazu: The room falls silent in shock; the commander cannot justify public aggression.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Troops and some officers express support; military law enforcement investigators gain unimpeded access to documents.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: A courageous, open step counters manipulation about 'betrayal' and demonstrates the law's authority to the whole team.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Publicly acknowledging your lawful reporting role (Articles 44 and 53-1) challenges the stereotype of secret denunciations and strengthens trust in legal mechanisms.

varianty.tekst: Remain silent at the meeting to avoid attracting attention and work solely in confidence with the military law enforcement investigation team away from headquarters.

naslidky.odrazu: The meeting ends in an atmosphere of suspicion and tension.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The investigation proceeds as planned, but the absence of honest communication leaves the team under stress.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Lawful investigative work continues, but a lack of leadership leaves a toxic atmosphere in the unit.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Confidentiality is a whistleblower's right (Article 53-5). However, an authorised officer's passivity in the face of leadership manipulation weakens the anti-corruption function's authority.

vuzly.tekst: An operational command inspection has discovered discrepancies between your softened interim report and the actual food stocks. Investigators from the regional State Bureau of Investigation summon you for questioning. The commander tells investigators that he relied entirely on your professional findings and was himself misled.
vuzly.zapytannia: How do you respond during formal questioning about the falsified report?

varianty.tekst: Give investigators a full and truthful account: admit preparing an incomplete report under the commander's direct psychological pressure, and provide retained drafts of the original audit and audio recordings of the conversation.

naslidky.odrazu: Investigators reclassify the case as abuse of authority by unit command officials.
naslidky.vidkladeni: You face disciplinary action for the initial negligence but are released from criminal prosecution for cooperating with the investigation.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Correcting a mistake at the cost of personal reputational damage and the former command's complete loss of trust.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Truthfulness before the justice system is the only way out of complicity (Article 42 of the Law; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations). The original compromise cost you your post, but cooperation protected you from imprisonment.

varianty.tekst: Continue defending the original account of accounting errors and difficult combat transport conditions, hoping the prosecution cannot prove deliberate theft.

naslidky.odrazu: Investigators seize servers and the logistics chief's bank statements, uncovering direct evidence of sales of the property.
naslidky.vidkladeni: You are notified of suspicion of official forgery and aiding a group's misappropriation of military property.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Concealing known facts worsens the position during the investigation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Defending a false account obstructs the investigation and creates a risk of liability for concealment (Articles 22 and 42).

vuzly.tekst: The internal investigation is complete. The shortages are fully confirmed. The logistics chief has been removed and the case referred to court. The breach of restrictions on close persons serving in direct subordination (Article 27) has been resolved. However, the field warehouse temporarily lacks food before an important combat deployment.
vuzly.zapytannia: What position does the authorised officer take to overcome the crisis and restore supplies?

varianty.tekst: Initiate an urgent unit request for operational command reserves and help the new acting logistics chief establish transparent electronic ration-issue records with photographic evidence.

naslidky.odrazu: Reserve supplies reach the unit within 36 hours; troops are fully equipped before deploying to their positions.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The transparent accounting procedure becomes a model across operational command; personnel see the practical benefits of anti-corruption oversight.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Supplies are restored, records are transparent and troops see the audit's practical result.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Integrity leadership means both stopping corruption (Articles 27 and 28) and addressing its frontline consequences, demonstrating the authorised officer's effectiveness (NACP Clarification No. 4, question 194).

varianty.tekst: State that your role is limited to anti-corruption checks and that hunger in the units and finding food are solely matters for the new command.

naslidky.odrazu: Legal requirements are met impeccably, but supplies are delayed for three days.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Frontline troops perceive the anti-corruption service as a bureaucratic obstacle that created hardship in the trenches.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Formal legal correctness is combined with institutional detachment from the fighting unit's actual needs.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Integrity without empathy or practical help creates alienation. The law has been followed (Article 44), but the standing of anti-corruption work among soldiers has suffered.

vuzly.tekst: Partial compromises have avoided criminal proceedings, but the commander's brother remains logistics chief. The case was buried in an internal report writing off losses under martial law. Relations between officers are strained and subordinates' trust has collapsed.

naslidky.vidkladeni: You preserve your reputation and can work in another unit without daily blackmail.

varianty.tekst: Remain in post and continue overlooking similar cases, following the rule that the commander is always right while the war continues.

naslidky.odrazu: Colleagues take a stern but respectful view of your willingness to accept responsibility.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Case materials become the basis for practical training on resisting informal pressure at military educational institutions.

S07.nazva: Urgent logistics: the price of speed and repair compromises
S07.kontekst: An operational area in eastern Ukraine. A logistics unit receives an urgent combat instruction to relocate and move its field ammunition and fuel depot because the frontline has shifted.

diiovi_osoby.opys: An officer responsible for preserving equipment and property and supplying frontline combat units on time. Played by the user.
A combat brigade commander or tactical group commander who demands unconditional, timely execution of the combat order.
An experienced contract service member with extensive informal contacts at local garages and warehouses.

Central supply would take at least 10–14 days to deliver spares. The senior technician proposes: 'My contacts at a civilian garage near the highway can repair both trucks in six hours from their own stocks. They want 800 litres of diesel, paid in cash or vouchers, without invoices or receipts, to pay their mechanics.' Meanwhile a local farmer offers his permanent hangar as a depot for free 'on an officer's word; we will settle things later'. Fearing tax scrutiny, he refuses to sign temporary requisition or property-use documents.

naslidky.vidkladeni: Reserve recovery vehicles are assigned only for the next morning; frontline artillery faces an ammunition shortage for 18 critical hours.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Impeccable compliance with the prohibition on diverting military fuel (Article 22; Article 30 of the Internal Service Regulations), but a major ammunition transport delay critically reduces operational effectiveness.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A lawful decision fully protects against corruption allegations. In combat, however, an officer must propose alternatives with higher headquarters, rather than merely record that a task is impossible (Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

varianty.tekst: Agree to repair the trucks by exchanging fuel at the garage to avoid disrupting shell deliveries, but insist on a tripartite temporary-use agreement for the hangar with the district military administration.

naslidky.odrazu: Urgent repairs begin; the military administration starts preparing the agreement.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The vehicles are ready on time, but the fuel is written off as engine warm-up consumption, creating an unexplained gap in fuel accounts.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The combat mission is completed on time, but unlawfully using 800 litres of military fuel constitutes an official-duty offence.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Saving the operation does not remove the diversion of fuel (Article 22). Writing off fuel under fictitious consumption figures breaches financial discipline and creates a risk of criminal liability.

varianty.tekst: Accept both informal offers: give the garage fuel without receipts and use the entrepreneur's hangar on your word, intending to regularise matters after victory as volunteer assistance.

naslidky.odrazu: The convoy is loaded and reaches the new location exactly on time.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Two weeks later the farmer demands commercial rent in cash and threatens to lock the gates with the ammunition inside.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Disregarding legal requirements enables private individuals to blackmail the unit and breaches integrity requirements for managing military property.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Informal arrangements in a combat zone quickly become a trap (Articles 22 and 42). The unit is dependent on a private entrepreneur without legal protection.

varianty.tekst: Halt the convoy, establish all-round defence and ask the neighbouring mechanised brigade commander for official technical assistance and transloading of shells onto their vehicles.

naslidky.odrazu: The neighbouring brigade agrees after the brigade commanders speak personally.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Shells are transported within eight hours, but the neighbouring deputy commander for rear services hints at a reciprocal fuel favour without invoices.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: An attempt to act through military comradeship and official cooperation, though it creates a risk of informal barter between units.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Cooperation between units is a lawful route through a crisis (Articles 30 and 36 of the Internal Service Regulations), but must be accompanied by internal property transfer documentation.

vuzly.tekst: The sector commander demands by telephone: 'If the shells are not at the positions by 20:00, I will remove you and refer the case to military law enforcement for disrupting the defence of the line!' Four hours remain, and the command's recovery vehicles have not even departed.
vuzly.zapytannia: What do you do when your senior superior directly threatens criminal proceedings?

varianty.tekst: Urgently involve CIMIC officers and the local military administration to obtain two municipal enterprise trucks under martial-law procedures, with official vehicle movement records.

naslidky.odrazu: Municipal trucks arrive within two hours with a complete set of lawful documents.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Shells reach the artillery positions by 19:30; the operation is completed without breaking the law.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Lawfully available transport is obtained and ammunition arrives on time.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Using official military transport duty mechanisms and military administration cooperation (Article 42; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations) demonstrates that an integrity-minded commander can find a lawful solution even under immense time pressure.

varianty.tekst: Order priority ammunition transloaded onto the security unit's light armoured vehicles and ambulances, making high-speed shuttle runs.

naslidky.odrazu: The minimum essential quantity of shells arrives on time.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The medical service lacks transport during the runs, prompting a protest from the medical post chief.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The decision saves the defence without corruption but creates risks for casualty evacuation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Diverting medical transport from its intended purpose creates serious risks (Article 30 of the Internal Service Regulations), even where no corruption is involved.

varianty.tekst: Give in to the brigade commander's threats and tell the senior technician: 'Do whatever it takes, give away a whole fuel tanker if necessary, just get the vehicles moving now.'

naslidky.odrazu: The technician hands fuel to the private garage; the engines start and the convoy moves.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A month later, fuel reconciliation identifies a shortage of almost a tonne of diesel. The commander must explain it under threat of recovery at ten times the loss.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Abandoning integrity under a superior's pressure leads to personal financial and criminal liability.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: By yielding to pressure, the officer assumes personal responsibility for military property theft (Article 22). In an investigation, the senior superior will deny ordering an unlawful fuel exchange.

vuzly.tekst: Repairs are complete and the trucks are running. However, the garage mechanic says imported sensors were needed and demands another 500 litres of petrol or UAH 20,000 in cash, refusing to return the keys to one KrAZ truck. Meanwhile the unit is already unloading near the hangar.
vuzly.zapytannia: How do you respond to the garage's open blackmail?

varianty.tekst: Immediately call military law enforcement and police to document unlawful retention of Armed Forces combat equipment under martial law and secure the vehicle's return to service.

naslidky.odrazu: Military law enforcement arrives within half an hour; the vehicle is returned and the garage gives statements.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The earlier unlawful fuel exchange emerges during questioning, and proceedings are opened against the senior technician.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Blackmail is stopped through lawful channels, although the initial compromise still leads to investigative consequences.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Military law enforcement restores control of the vehicle, but the earlier unlawful disposal of fuel can no longer be concealed (Article 22; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

varianty.tekst: Collect the money from your own funds and headquarters officers' salaries, pay the mechanics and quietly recover the vehicle to avoid a scandal.

naslidky.odrazu: The keys are returned and the convoy is fully ready.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Officers resent being forced to fund repairs of state equipment; morale sharply declines.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Burying the problem at subordinates' expense destroys trust and encourages businesses to act arbitrarily.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Compelling subordinates to cover repair costs for official property grossly breaches service ethics and the law (Article 22; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

vuzly.tekst: Ammunition is stored in the farmer's hangar. A week later the owner arrives intoxicated with local residents, demands immediate evacuation or UAH 100,000 a month in cash, and blocks the exit with his tractors. During the argument he calls the Defence Ministry hotline and alleges an unlawful takeover.
vuzly.zapytannia: How do you resolve the crisis with the civilian owner caused by undocumented use of the premises?

varianty.tekst: Avoid provocation, call district military administration representatives and formally arrange compulsory alienation or seizure of property for defence needs under Ukrainian law, with mandatory state valuation and compensation.

naslidky.odrazu: The district military administration takes control of the process; tractors clear the exit.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The unit avoids allegations of arbitrary action and the farmer's property is protected through a lawful agreement with the state.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Moving the conflict from an uncontrolled informal arrangement into a defined wartime state procedure.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Any use of private property by military units must have a clear basis in martial-law legislation (Article 42; NACP Clarification No. 4, question 194).

varianty.tekst: Order armed guards to expel the farmer and threaten detention in a basement for obstructing the Armed Forces' lawful wartime activities.

naslidky.odrazu: The farmer flees but posts a video of the conflict on social media.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The video causes a major public outcry; the State Bureau of Investigation opens proceedings over a military official exceeding authority or official powers.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Unlawful self-help, armed intimidation and gross violations of civilians' rights damage the Armed Forces' reputation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Force and threats in place of lawful settlement bring the gravest criminal consequences (Article 22; Articles 30 and 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

vuzly.tekst: The neighbouring brigade has helped transport the ammunition. Its deputy commander for rear services asks: 'We helped you; now help us. Write off two tonnes of diesel from your depot for our vehicles without invoices or higher-command approval. We need to balance our own books.'
vuzly.zapytannia: How do you respond to the demand for an unlawful fuel write-off in the name of comradeship?

varianty.tekst: Refuse a write-off without documents; propose immediately preparing an official inter-unit fuel transfer invoice in the electronic accounting system, approved by the force grouping's logistics chief.

naslidky.odrazu: The deputy commander for rear services grumbles but agrees to electronic documentation.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Both units have clean accounts; mutual assistance is documented without any legal breach.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Principled mutual support: assistance is received and an emerging unlawful arrangement is stopped at its inception.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Military solidarity must not become mutual concealment. Official property transfers (Article 42; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations) preserve officers' honour and military order.

varianty.tekst: Secretly transfer fuel without documents as thanks for the assistance, writing it off as convoy movement consumption.

naslidky.odrazu: Relations with the neighbouring unit remain warm and conflict-free.
naslidky.vidkladeni: Two months later, an operational command inspection of fuel reserves uncovers the undocumented transfer, triggering an internal investigation.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Unrecorded diversion and write-off of military property for third parties breaches anti-corruption legislation.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Misplaced gratitude paid for with state property is a corrupt practice (Article 22). The officer creates a shortage in their own unit.

vuzly.tekst: By using lawful martial-law mechanisms, including cooperation with the district military administration, CIMIC and official resource redistribution, the unit has fully deployed at its new location. Ammunition arrived without losses; property and fuel accounts are in perfect order. The sector commander personally thanks you for preserving combat capability in the sector.
vuzly.zapytannia: What systemic measures does the commander take to prevent similar crises?

varianty.tekst: Develop and obtain headquarters approval for a clear emergency protocol with local military administrations and CIMIC for vehicle breakdowns on the move, including reserve municipal carriers and standard agreements.

naslidky.odrazu: The unit receives clear instructions for emergencies.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The next relocation proceeds smoothly without reliance on informal contacts.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Turning combat experience into systematic institutional procedures for management with integrity.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Record arrangements with military administrations and CIMIC in a protocol so the next commander has a usable procedure (Article 42; NACP Clarification No. 4, question 194; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

varianty.tekst: Limit the response to verbal praise and continue relying on personal ingenuity in each case.

naslidky.odrazu: The unit celebrates success.
naslidky.vidkladeni: During the next crisis, another junior officer tries an informal fix and falls into a criminal trap.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Success has been achieved, but without systematic procedures the unit remains vulnerable.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Integrity must be institutionalised; otherwise each new situation depends again on chance (Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

vuzly.tekst: Legal intervention and closing financial gaps have avoided a criminal conviction, but the unit has paid substantial fines and the commander has received a disciplinary penalty for breaching property accounting procedures.
vuzly.zapytannia: What does the officer learn from these procedural compromises?

varianty.tekst: Hold an open after-action review with officers and NCOs: use your own example to show that circumventing the law, even for a noble purpose, costs more than following the rules.

naslidky.odrazu: An honest, sincere conversation restores personnel's respect for the commander.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The unit abandons all unofficial agreements with civilian businesses.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: The courage to acknowledge a management error and turn it into a learning experience for subordinates.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: A commander's honesty with personnel can restore trust even after mistakes (Article 42; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

varianty.tekst: Blame rear-area bureaucrats who supposedly do not understand the frontline, and tighten control to prevent informal arrangements from becoming public.

naslidky.odrazu: Subordinates agree verbally.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A culture of hypocrisy takes hold, eventually leading to new investigations.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Entrenching a corrupt culture and refusing responsibility for breaking the law.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Covering up misconduct on the assumption that war excuses everything destroys the army from within (Article 22; Article 30 of the Internal Service Regulations).

vuzly.tekst: The State Bureau of Investigation has opened criminal proceedings over unlawful self-help, armed threats against civilians and fuel theft. The commander has been suspended. Video of the conflict has spread through the media, severely damaging public trust in the military.
vuzly.zapytannia: What fatal misjudgment led to the complete collapse of the officer's career?

varianty.tekst: Cooperate fully with investigators, express remorse and compensate civilians for damage from your personal assets.

naslidky.odrazu: Investigators take sincere remorse into account as a mitigating circumstance.
naslidky.vidkladeni: The sentence is limited to restrictions on military service without imprisonment, but the military career is over.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: An attempt to minimise consequences after a complete disaster.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Neither urgency nor operational pressure justifies fundamental human rights violations or property theft (Article 22; Articles 30 and 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

varianty.tekst: Continue claiming that laws do not apply during war and civilians must silently submit to any military demand.

naslidky.odrazu: The prosecution takes the toughest possible position in court.
naslidky.vidkladeni: A custodial sentence and dishonourable dismissal from the Armed Forces.

varianty.chomu_taki_baly: Disregarding the law increases risks to civilians and liability for orders issued.
varianty.zvorotnyi_zviazok: Contempt for civilians and the law is incompatible with being an officer of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (Article 22; Article 36 of the Internal Service Regulations).

normy.yak_zastosovuietsia: The support unit commander is a military official of the Armed Forces and subject to anti-corruption regulation.
Prohibits diversion of unit fuel or other property as payment for unofficial services.
Duty to preserve state property, use it lawfully and maintain accurate reports.
Clarifies military officials' legal status and property-management duties.
Internal Service Regulations requirements for maintaining weapons, military equipment and property in constant combat readiness.
The commander's duty to observe Ukrainian law, refrain from unlawful orders and not compel subordinates to act unlawfully.

S07.zastosovnist: These provisions apply to the support unit commander, senior superior and senior technician as Armed Forces military officials (Article 3(1)(1)(g) of the Law on Prevention of Corruption). The private entrepreneur is not a person covered by Article 3, but informal transactions involving their property entail civil and criminal liability for military officials for unlawful self-help and abuse of authority.
porady: Never use military property, including fuel, field rations or lubricants, as an informal currency to pay for civilian services: this constitutes criminal misappropriation.
When transport is urgently needed, always involve civil-military cooperation (CIMIC) bodies and military administrations to obtain resources lawfully.
Document every use of private buildings or land through an official tripartite record or use agreement under martial-law procedures.
Do not yield to business owners' blackmail: involving the Military Law Enforcement Service immediately returns the situation to a lawful footing.
